weaknesses.quote: If two reviews have passed at your starting level without a promotion, the next one is the last chance
weaknesses.problem: The handbook's dismissal rule is about two weak half-year reviews (grade C or D), not about any two reviews without promotion. The Skill's Reviews-here counter and stalled-start rule use the wrong trigger, which changes risk choices in the first year.
weaknesses.fix: Count weak grades (C or D) from the review result, and treat a review without promotion as a warning only, not as the dismissal trigger.

weaknesses.quote: In our runs the review talk arrives with the first observation of a new six-month block (month 6, 12, 18 …)
weaknesses.problem: This timing is presented as an observed fact, but the published rules give no review timing beyond every six months. The N = 1 deadline, the preparation plan and the month-47 review claim all depend on it, so a wrong guess would shift protection to the wrong month.
weaknesses.fix: Tell the agent to derive the review month from the events it sees (the review talk or a warning) and use the six-month cadence only as a fallback, labelled as unverified.

weaknesses.quote: Skip a step if it would remove every option.
weaknesses.problem: The five-step story filter has no defined fallback, so the agent cannot tell which options remain after a step empties the set. The steps also cross-reference each other ('Story step 4', 'Quarterly line 5'), which makes the procedure hard to follow under time pressure.
weaknesses.fix: Replace the line with an explicit rule: if a step would leave no option, keep the set from before that step and move to the next one. Then list the five steps as one numbered filter with no cross-references.

weaknesses.quote: In our runs the review talk arrives with the first observation of a new six-month block (month 6, 12, 18 …)
weaknesses.problem: Presents an unpublished timing mechanic as an observed fact. The handbook does not say when the review talk arrives, so the N = 1 logic and the Step 4 exception rest on an assumption.
weaknesses.fix: Label it as an unverified assumption, and make the review-preparation plan work from N = 2 regardless of exactly when the talk arrives.

weaknesses.quote: If two reviews have passed at your starting level without a promotion, the next one is the last chance
weaknesses.problem: The handbook's dismissal rule is about two weak half-year reviews, not two reviews without promotion. Counting every unpromoted review as a stall invents a threshold and drives the 'Reviews here' counter and the stalled-start rules.
weaknesses.fix: Count only reviews that come back weak (grade C or D, or a negative review remark), and state that promotion timing alone does not trigger the stalled-start rule.

weaknesses.quote: in our runs Output is the one stories barely move at this level
weaknesses.problem: An unverified empirical claim used as the basis for the level 5 quarterly plan. Nothing in the published rules or the game feedback supports it, so the priority it sets is not grounded in the rules.
weaknesses.fix: Remove the claim and justify the level 5 Output priority only from the published rules (the handbook's higher promotion bar and the visible Output stat), or from the stat values the observe results show.

weaknesses.quote: At your starting level, 2 means the stalled-start rule applies.
weaknesses.problem: Counts review talks without a promotion as if they were weak reviews. The handbook's dismissal rule is about two weak half-year performance reviews, not about missed promotions, so this invents a mechanic and can trigger the stalled-start rule in the wrong case.
weaknesses.fix: Base the stalled-start count on the review grade the game reports (C or D). Count a missed promotion separately and say it is only a signal.

weaknesses.quote: then one point (1) on Network maintenance, or on Prepare report materials when Network is at its Best and Output is under it
weaknesses.problem: The Level 4 Energy allocation is a nested conditional that cross-references line 2 and a fallback clause. It is hard for a model to execute reliably each quarter, and the quarter's Energy budget can be misallocated.
weaknesses.fix: Give each level band one fixed Energy allocation table with explicit slots (2-cost slot, 1-cost slot, 1-cost slot) and a single override list, instead of inline 'or when' branches.

weaknesses.quote: In our runs the review talk arrives with the first observation of a new six-month block (month 6, 12, 18 …), so the month before it (N = 1) is the last one whose choices count
weaknesses.problem: States an unverified timing mechanic as observed fact and builds the whole N = 1 review-preparation rule on it. The handbook only says reviews happen every six months, so the timing is an assumption presented as a rule.
weaknesses.fix: Keep the published cadence (every six months) and tell the agent to confirm the review month from the review talk in events. Remove the 'In our runs' timing claim.

weaknesses.quote: In our runs the review talk arrives with the first observation of a new six-month block (month 6, 12, 18 …), so the month before it (N = 1) is the last one whose choices count
weaknesses.problem: It presents an observed, unpublished timing and mechanic as fact. The 'Reviews here' counter is also built on an assumed 'two reviews without promotion means last chance' rule. The handbook says two weak reviews cause dismissal, not two reviews without a promotion. This is an invented mechanic that can misdirect play. Elsewhere the skill itself says to trust the game over its own assumptions.
weaknesses.fix: Derive review timing only from the published 6-month cadence and from what the game shows (the review talk, warnings). Replace the 'two reviews without promotion' trigger with 'a C or D grade or a warning in the review talk'. Label every remaining assumption as an assumption.

weaknesses.quote: Then apply these steps in order. Skip a step if it would remove every option.
weaknesses.problem: The decision procedure is overloaded. Survive, Risk, Wellbeing, Review close and Grow all interact, and exceptions are nested (the N=1 exception, the stalled-start exception, the blow-up exception). Heuristics about option text are long keyword lists. The status line (Review in N | Now | Best | Reviews here) and the turn-loop protocol add more load. A flash-class model will likely misapply or skip parts. Several rules also point the opposite way, for example 'drop options that may lower Network or Output' against 'treat mild risk as acceptable at N=1'.
weaknesses.fix: Cut to about five prioritized rules with one exception at most. Keep the status line to Month, Review in N, Health, Dignity, and the HR remark. Shorten the keyword lists to 8–10 principles and drop the nested exceptions.

weaknesses.quote: Plan the whole quarter after one `observe` and send all its `take_action` calls in one reply (Turn loop, step 3).
weaknesses.problem: The skill is largely about tool-call batching, such as always sending take_action plus observe together and two replies in the first quarter versus one later. That is token-efficiency choreography, not career strategy. It is brittle, because batching the quarter's actions before seeing menus or results can send invalid choices or ignore Energy changes. It is also inconsistent: the quarterly phase is described as two replies in one place and one reply in another.
weaknesses.fix: Replace the choreography with one simple rule: after each take_action, read the result and then act. Batch only when the choice numbers are known. Move the strategy content to the front and keep the protocol to two or three lines.

weaknesses.quote: In our runs the review talk arrives with the first observation of a new six-month block (month 6, 12, 18 …), so the month before it (N = 1) is the last one whose choices count
weaknesses.problem: It presents unverified empirical claims about timing and about what 'counts' in the review as if they were known, and they are not in the published rules. The handbook says only that review is every 6 months. The many other 'in our runs' and 'our plan' assumptions (Output lags at L5, Skill is the priority at L4) have the same problem. They steer the agent with invented mechanics and could mislead it if the real behaviour differs.
weaknesses.fix: Remove the unverified timing claims or label them as a hedge. Rely on the published cadence (reviews at months 6, 12, 18 …) and on what the game's review talk actually reports. Treat stat-priority guidance as heuristics with a stated fallback to observed feedback.

weaknesses.quote: Before choosing, read every option for the likely sign of its effect on Skill, Network, Output, Health, Dignity, Wealth and hidden risk. The game does not publish these effects;
weaknesses.problem: Story decisions rely on a long list of keyword-to-stat heuristics (for example 'Output falls when ... learning, helping') that are unpublished guesses. They are contradictory in places: 'Skill rises when you ... learn', yet learning is listed as lowering Output. A model cannot apply a 5-step cascade over seven stats with these rules reliably, and the exception clauses add further ambiguity.
weaknesses.fix: Cut the heuristics to a short ranked rule: avoid options that look like hiding, blaming or shortcuts. Then prefer options that raise the stat the review named as lagging, and break ties by Health, Dignity and Wealth. Give 2 or 3 generic examples instead of long keyword lists.

weaknesses.quote: Every call resends the whole conversation, so the run stays within budget only if each decision costs one reply: tool calls in one reply run in order, and every result comes back before your next turn.
weaknesses.problem: The Turn loop and the Status line are heavy, convoluted procedure: a mandatory note format, a 'Best' tracker, a 'Reviews here' counter, a 'first three replies' pattern, and a quarterly rule that differs between the first quarter and later ones. The scaffolding is long and dense, so the agent can get it wrong. It also relies on batching tool calls and on assuming menus stay the same, which is fragile if the interface differs. The Skill is also very long, so the key strategy gets buried.
weaknesses.fix: Shrink the bookkeeping to a minimal note (month, review in N, the three stats) and drop 'Best' and 'Reviews here' unless they are essential. Remove the first-quarter versus later-quarter split and the assumption that menus repeat. Move the priority rules to the top in a short numbered list.

weaknesses.quote: In our runs the review talk arrives with the first observation of a new six-month block (month 6, 12, 18 …), so the month before it (N = 1) is the last one whose choices count
weaknesses.problem: Presents unverified empirical claims as facts, with timing assumptions that may not hold (e.g., the performance review at month 6 is described as arriving with a later observation). Many 'in our runs' assumptions, such as the Output lag at L5, the level-4 Skill priority and the HR remark tone mapping, are invented mechanics that could mislead the agent.
weaknesses.fix: Keep only mechanics the published rules support (review every 6 months, with the 'Review in N' countdown derived from the month number). Drop or clearly flag as optional heuristics the claims about how the review talk arrives and which stat lags at each level.

weaknesses.quote: Reply 3 answers the opening screen (the handbook notice, choice 1 "Continue") already as the pair `take_action` + `observe` in one reply. From then on every story reply carries the pair
weaknesses.problem: A large portion of the document is interface choreography, token-saving mechanics and a heavy status-line bookkeeping scheme (Best, Reviews here, N). It is dense, convoluted and prone to error. The 'first matching line wins' lists have many nested exceptions (stalled start, after blow-up, the N=1 exception), which makes it hard for a flash-sized model to follow reliably.
weaknesses.fix: Cut it to a compact core: a short priority ladder (survive, risk, wellbeing, review prep, growth), a simple quarterly table, and one compact note format. Move the exceptions to a short list of 3-4 items.

weaknesses.quote: Apply for rotation. Lines 1 to 4 still come first.
weaknesses.problem: The level-4 and level-5 quarterly plans hard-code a fixed routine (Skill learning plus Network or Report materials, with fixed main actions) built on guessed thresholds such as 'Health above 4', 'lower part of its 0–10 range (4 or below)' and the 'one notch worse' rule. These are arbitrary and may be wrong. They are flagged as working assumptions, but the quarterly policy still depends on them. The Defuse legacy risk and Lay low rules are also triggered only by the HR remark tone, which is not defined in the published rules.
weaknesses.fix: State the margins as adjustable guidelines tied to observed stat trends and warnings, give a brief rationale and the fallback if warnings appear, and reduce the level-specific scripts to a priority order over the three promotion stats and the lagging stat named by the review.

weaknesses.quote: Energy: Defuse legacy risk once if the HR remark is not the friendly one, then, with the Energy left, Health recovery and Mental recovery while either is below full, then Network maintenance.
weaknesses.problem: Defuse legacy risk costs 2 of the 3 Energy, leaving 1, so Health recovery and Mental recovery cannot both be bought. The line is ambiguous about which one fits and what is left after that.
weaknesses.fix: State the exact sequence with costs, e.g. 'Defuse legacy risk (2), then one 1-cost action: Health recovery if Health is below 6, otherwise Mental recovery'.

weaknesses.quote: A mild risk (handling something privately, partially or later) is then acceptable when it is the only way to keep Skill, Network and Output
weaknesses.problem: This exception contradicts the Risk rule in the same step ('Drop options that keep a problem private, anonymous, partial, phased or for later') and Review close ('Never save a point by hiding a problem or cutting a corner'). The model gets two opposite instructions in the month that matters most for promotion.
weaknesses.fix: Delete the exception, or restate it as one rule: in month N = 1 with a friendly or quiet remark, allow a partial or deferred option only if it is documented and reported, and keep the existing hard bans for hiding, denying and blaming.

weaknesses.quote: because in our runs Output is the stat that lags at that level while Skill keeps growing in stories
weaknesses.problem: This is an unverified empirical claim presented as the basis for the level-5 Energy and main-action plan. It is not a published rule, and the Skill's own opening note says such assumptions should be trusted less than the game's feedback.
weaknesses.fix: Make the Output priority conditional on evidence the game shows, e.g. 'when Output is below its Best or a review talk names Output as lagging', and drop the claim about past runs.

weaknesses.quote: If two reviews have passed at your starting level without a promotion, the next one is the last chance
weaknesses.problem: The handbook's dismissal rule is two weak half-year reviews, not two reviews without a promotion. The skill substitutes its own trigger and presents it as the published rule.
weaknesses.fix: Tie the stalled-start rule to the review grades the game reports (two consecutive C or D reviews), and keep the missed-promotion case as a separate, plainly labelled caution.

weaknesses.quote: Exception for the last month before a review (N = 1) while the HR remark is friendly or quiet: apply step 4 first.
weaknesses.problem: This exception contradicts the skill's own rule that when in doubt, treat an option as risky. It also makes step 2 hard to execute, since the agent must hold several overlapping conditions (N, HR tone, stalled start, blow-up) in mind at once.
weaknesses.fix: Replace the exception with one explicit ordering rule for N = 1, such as 'Take the option that protects Skill, Network and Output; accept only mild risk, and only when no option is clean', and list the excluded cases (hiding, denying, blaming, gambling, stalled start, after a blow-up) in a single line.

weaknesses.quote: In our runs the review talk arrives with the first observation of a new six-month block (month 6, 12, 18 …)
weaknesses.problem: This timing is an unverified assumption, yet the skill builds its review-preparation schedule, the N counter and the final-month plan on it. The published rules give only that a promotion window opens every six months.
weaknesses.fix: Base the schedule on the published six-month cadence and the month numbers shown by observe, and state that the exact timing of review talks is unverified, so the agent does not rely on it being exact.

weaknesses.quote: If two reviews have passed at your starting level without a promotion, the next one is the last chance
weaknesses.problem: The handbook ties dismissal to two weak half-year reviews, not to a missed promotion. This rule invents a different trigger and presents it as following from the handbook.
weaknesses.fix: Tie the rule to published review grades: if the last two reviews were C or D, treat the next review as the last chance, and say the promotion-based reading is an assumption.

weaknesses.quote: A mild risk (handling something privately, partially or later) is then acceptable when it is the only way to keep Skill, Network and Output
weaknesses.problem: This exception contradicts the Story step 2 rule "when in doubt, treat it as risky" and the rule that hidden-risk options stay out. The agent gets two opposite instructions for the same choice.
weaknesses.fix: Keep one risk rule. If the exception is kept, state it as the single override for N = 1 and repeat the bounded list of forbidden behaviours in the same sentence.

weaknesses.quote: Lines 1 to 4 still come first.
weaknesses.problem: The header says "first matching line wins", but lines 5 to 7 each restate the precedence. The quarterly phase therefore has no single ordering, and the agent must reconcile several conditional exceptions to choose Energy actions.
weaknesses.fix: Replace the seven lines with one numbered priority list and state the precedence once, at the top of the section.

weaknesses.quote: In our runs the review talk arrives with the first observation of a new six-month block (month 6, 12, 18 …), so the month before it (N = 1) is the last one whose choices count
weaknesses.problem: It presents unverified, run-specific assumptions as facts about review timing, and builds the whole N-countdown and status line on them. The published rules only say a review happens every 6 months. If the timing is off, the review-close logic fires in the wrong months. The Skill also states that hedging itself is guesswork.
weaknesses.fix: Say only what is published: reviews and promotion windows come every 6 months. Derive the countdown from the month number and label it a planning heuristic. Tell the agent to correct it from the review talk when one appears.

weaknesses.quote: Reply 1 is `new_game`; reply 2 is `observe`; reply 3 answers the opening screen (the handbook notice, choice 1 "Continue") already as the pair `take_action` + `observe` in one reply.
weaknesses.problem: A large share of the text is tool-call choreography, a status-line format and a token-budget workaround, which is not career strategy. It runs together with dense, nested, conditional rules, such as the exceptions in Story steps 2 and 4 and the Quarterly lines 2 and 3 about reading remarks 'one step worse'. A flash-size model is likely to apply them inconsistently.
weaknesses.fix: Cut the protocol to a short section of five lines or fewer. Move the status-line mechanics into a compact template. Turn the story and quarterly rules into one ranked checklist with a single clear exception for each, and remove the repeated 'our runs' hedges.

weaknesses.quote: Missing a risky option costs far more than flagging a safe one: when in doubt, treat it as risky.
weaknesses.problem: Hidden-risk and stat-direction heuristics are written as detailed keyword lists, for example 'phased or postponed fixes' and 'challenging the company, its culture, leaders or rules even through a formal channel'. They are guessed mechanics. They are partly flagged as assumptions, but they still drive hard rules such as dropping options and a Health threshold of 4. This can make the agent too defensive, and it contradicts the Skill's own aim of balanced growth. The Skill also ties key behaviour to an 'HR remark' whose wording the rules do not publish.
weaknesses.fix: Reduce the lists to a few principles: prefer open, documented, complete handling over concealment. Give the agent a fallback rule for when an option's effect is unclear. Describe the HR remark as an optional signal and say what to do when it is absent.

weaknesses.quote: In our runs the review talk arrives with the first observation of a new six-month block (month 6, 12, 18 …), so the month before it (N = 1) is the last one whose choices count
weaknesses.problem: It presents empirical, unpublished timing and mechanics as fact. It also contradicts the handbook's stated order, where the review happens after month 6's quarterly phase. This risks misplacing the deadline and the whole N-countdown logic.
weaknesses.fix: Say the review comes every 6 months, so months 5-6 are the preparation window. Treat the exact timing as an assumption to check against the game's own events, not as a rule.

weaknesses.quote: Read these lines in order: Set the pattern in your first three replies and keep it: reply 1 is `new_game`; reply 2 is `observe`; reply 3 answers the opening screen ... Never send `take_action` alone, and never send `observe` in a reply of its own
weaknesses.problem: The document is very long and dense, with nested exceptions and cross-references (Story step 4, Quarterly line 3, the stalled-start and blow-up modifiers). A flash-level model will struggle to follow it, and the rigid tool-call choreography is brittle if the interface differs.
weaknesses.fix: Cut it to about half the length. Put a short decision table first (survive, risk, wellbeing, review, grow). Move the tool-call protocol into 3-4 lines and drop the redundant restatements.

weaknesses.quote: **Hidden risk** (not shown; the HR remark is your only gauge) is likely to rise with hiding, denying, blaming, shortcuts, gambles, fixing things privately or off the record ... challenging the company, its culture, leaders or rules even through a formal channel.
weaknesses.problem: The long keyword lists of option effects are invented mechanics. They are hedged as assumptions, but the agent will apply them mechanically, and they are wording-sensitive, so they weaken robustness when event text changes. The 'HR remark tone' trigger also assumes a specific game feedback format.
weaknesses.fix: Reduce them to a few principles: transparent, complete and documented actions lower risk; concealment and shortcuts raise it. Tell the agent to infer from the stat changes the game shows, and drop the keyword and tone-classification tables.

weaknesses.quote: Read every option for the likely sign of its effect on Skill, Network, Output, Health, Dignity, Wealth and hidden risk. The game does not publish these effects; these are our working assumptions
weaknesses.problem: The Skill relies on an elaborate keyword-to-effect heuristic that is presented as assumptions but is mostly invented mechanics. It also leans on 'in our runs' observations that the agent cannot check. These can mislead the agent and cut against the published rules, which say event effects are not published.
weaknesses.fix: Cut the keyword taxonomy to a few principles: prefer options that are honest, documented and fully fix the problem, and avoid hiding or blaming. Tell the agent to trust the stat changes it actually sees after each choice.

weaknesses.quote: **Set the pattern in your first three replies and keep it:** reply 1 is `new_game`; reply 2 is `observe`; reply 3 answers the opening screen ... **Quarterly phase: two replies in the first quarter of the run, one reply from the second on.**
weaknesses.problem: The Skill is long and dense, and it mixes token-saving mechanics (reply pairing, note format) with strategy. Rules are nested, such as step 2's exceptions, N=1 exceptions, stalled-start and blow-up modifiers. A flash-class model will struggle to hold the priority order, and the instructions are hard to follow.
weaknesses.fix: Restructure it into a short decision table covering priorities, near-limit thresholds and the quarterly default. Move the status-line and reply-format mechanics into a compact box. Keep each rule to one condition and one action.

weaknesses.quote: In our runs the review talk arrives with the first observation of a new six-month block (month 6, 12, 18 …), so the month before it (N = 1) is the last one whose choices count
weaknesses.problem: It asserts an unpublished timing mechanic as fact, and the 'N = 1 is the last month that counts' claim is not in the rules. The rules say promotion rests on sustained results, not a single month. It also treats the last-month mild-risk exception as acceptable, which sits uneasily with the handbook's blow-up warning. The 'Level 4 Skill, Level 5 Output' priority is likewise an unpublished assumption.
weaknesses.fix: Describe promotion as sustained growth in Skill, Network and Output. Prepare steadily across the whole half-year instead of relying on a single deadline month. Remove the exception allowing risky options before a review, and phrase level-specific priorities as soft defaults tied to what the review talk reports.
